To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crucial steps in the direction of symbol processing in PDP models lie in incorporating an Episodic Short-Term Memory for serial order information (ESM) and a Selective Attention Mechanism (SAM) in PDP models, and that a new model which incorporates these mechanisms is a promising step to develop a cognitive architecture of power and generativity comparable to ACT* and SOA

(1) the binding problem can be solved with a neurally inspired model of timing in the brain; (2) this model can be used to implement a flexible short term episodic memory; (3) the episodic memory can be used to solve the problem of binding in PDP models; and (4) a PDP model with episodic memory can implement a selective attention mechanism.
PDP models are good for representing and manipulating knowledge and that they are poor at representing and manipulating symbols.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of cognitive architectures which integrate the best features of PDP models and physical symbol systems.

the construction of a cognitive architecture that combines the strengths of parallel distributed processing and symbolic processing, which can be used for the development of cognitive models in cognitive psychology and cognitive science.
the construction of an integrated cognitive model which is based on the principles of PDP models and incorporates a flexible short term store for episodic memory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a model which incorporates episodic short term memories and selective attention is necessary and sufficient for the implementation of a symbol manipulation system.
the binding problem is the key to the integration of PDP models and symbol manipulation.
PDP and symbolic models are both necessary for a complete model of human cognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an architecture which is able to perform the basic functions of a physical symbol system.
we are able to combine the advantages of both PDP and symbol manipulation in one model.
PDP models are not poor at symbol manipulation, but rather they have to be modified in a way to make them suitable for symbolic manipulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to build models that are capable of symbolic manipulation and that are also biologically plausible.
PDP models can indeed be made to be as powerful as symbol manipulation models.
the binding problem is not a problem of the binding itself, but a problem of the representation of serial order information in PDP models.
